collection.title: Class 10 Practical Science Viva Voce Prep
collection.description: Exemplar viva voce question bank for CBSE Class 10 practical experiments featuring model answers, difficulty filters, and interactive Quiz Me practice mode.
collection.scopeLabel: 96 Practical Viva Questions across 8 CBSE Science Experiments — Class 10

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What gas is liberated when dilute HCl reacts with sodium carbonate?

metadata.modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide gas (CO₂) is liberated with brisk effervescence.
metadata.examinerTip: Always mention 'brisk effervescence' along with the chemical formula CO₂.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does lime water turn milky when CO₂ gas is passed through it?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because CO₂ reacts with lime water [Ca(OH)₂] to form an insoluble white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).
metadata.examinerTip: Give the balanced equation: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What happens if CO₂ gas is passed through lime water for a prolonged time?

metadata.modelAnswer: The milky white solution becomes clear transparent again because insoluble CaCO₃ converts into water-soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate [Ca(HCO₃)₂].
metadata.examinerTip: Equation: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂ (soluble).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: How do Na₂CO₃ and NaHCO₃ differ in their molar gas yield when reacted with excess HCl?

metadata.modelAnswer: 1 mole of Na₂CO₃ requires 2 moles of HCl to yield 1 mole of CO₂, while 1 mole of NaHCO₃ requires only 1 mole of HCl to yield 1 mole of CO₂.
metadata.examinerTip: Check stoichometric coefficients in balanced equations.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the chemical formula and common name of Na₂CO₃·10H₂O?

metadata.modelAnswer: The common name is Washing Soda, and its formula is hydrated Sodium Carbonate decahydrate (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O).
metadata.examinerTip: Anhydrous Na₂CO₃ is called soda ash.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is NaHCO₃ used as an active ingredient in antacid tablets?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because NaHCO₃ is a mild non-corrosive basic salt that neutralizes excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
metadata.examinerTip: Mention mild basic nature so it does not irritate tissues.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does CO₂ extinguish a burning candle flame?

metadata.modelAnswer: CO₂ is denser than air and does not support combustion; it blankets the fuel, cutting off oxygen supply.
metadata.examinerTip: Mention non-supporter of combustion property.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why must the lower end of the thistle funnel dip below the liquid level in the test tube?

metadata.modelAnswer: To prevent the evolved CO₂ gas from escaping back through the thistle funnel into the atmosphere instead of going through the delivery tube.
metadata.examinerTip: Forming a liquid seal is crucial.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Can dilute H₂SO₄ be substituted for dilute HCl in this carbonate experiment?

metadata.modelAnswer: Yes, dilute H₂SO₄ also reacts with Na₂CO₃ to liberate CO₂ and form soluble Na₂SO₄.
metadata.examinerTip: Note: avoid using H₂SO₄ with insoluble carbonates like CaCO₃ due to surface coating.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: How do you distinguish between CO₂ gas and SO₂ gas in the lab?

metadata.modelAnswer: Both turn lime water milky, but SO₂ turns acidified potassium dichromate paper from orange to green, whereas CO₂ has no effect.
metadata.examinerTip: SO₂ also has a pungent choking sulfur smell.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Is Na₂CO₃ an acidic, basic, or neutral salt?

metadata.modelAnswer: It is a basic salt because it is formed by the reaction of a strong base (NaOH) with a weak acid (H₂CO₃).
metadata.examinerTip: Salt of Strong Base + Weak Acid = Basic Salt (pH > 7).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What chemical change occurs when solid NaHCO₃ is heated strongly?

metadata.modelAnswer: It decomposes into sodium carbonate, water vapor, and carbon dioxide gas: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.
metadata.examinerTip: This reaction causes cake dough to rise in baking.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What does 'pH' stand for and what does it measure?

metadata.modelAnswer: 'pH' stands for 'potenz' (power in German) of Hydrogen. It measures the concentration of H⁺ ions in a solution.
metadata.examinerTip: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺].

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is a universal indicator and how does it differ from litmus paper?

metadata.modelAnswer: Universal indicator is a mixture of several organic dyes that shows a continuous range of different colors over pH 1 to 14, whereas litmus only indicates acidic or basic state.
metadata.examinerTip: Universal indicator gives relative strength, litmus gives binary acid/base test.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is the pH of lemon juice around 2.2?

metadata.modelAnswer: Lemon juice contains high concentrations of citric acid and ascorbic acid (Vitamin C).
metadata.examinerTip: Citric acid is a tricarboxylic organic acid.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Can a solution have a negative pH value?

metadata.modelAnswer: Yes, extremely concentrated strong acids (e.g. 2M or 12M HCl) have [H⁺] > 1 M, resulting in negative pH values (e.g., -log(2) = -0.3).
metadata.examinerTip: pH scale is not strictly bounded between 0 and 14.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the pH of pure distilled water at 25°C?

metadata.modelAnswer: It is exactly 7.0 (neutral) because [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M.
metadata.examinerTip: K_w = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: At what pH level does tooth enamel start decaying in the mouth?

metadata.modelAnswer: Tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) begins to corrode when mouth pH drops below 5.5 due to acid-producing bacteria.
metadata.examinerTip: Toothpaste is basic to neutralize this acid.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: How do farmers treat overly acidic soil with low pH?

metadata.modelAnswer: They add quicklime (CaO), slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂], or chalk (CaCO₃) to neutralize excessive soil acidity.
metadata.examinerTip: Liming soil restores optimal agricultural pH (~6.5-7.5).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What happens to the pH of an acidic solution when it is diluted with water?

metadata.modelAnswer: The pH increases towards 7 because [H⁺] ion concentration decreases upon dilution.
metadata.examinerTip: It never exceeds 7 no matter how much water is added.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does 0.1M HCl have a lower pH (~1) than 0.1M CH₃COOH (~3)?

metadata.modelAnswer: HCl is a strong acid that completely dissociates into H⁺ ions, whereas CH₃COOH is a weak acid that dissociates only partially (~1%).
metadata.examinerTip: Higher [H⁺] concentration directly translates to lower numerical pH value.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the threshold pH value below which rain is classified as Acid Rain?

metadata.modelAnswer: Rainfall with a pH less than 5.6 is classified as Acid Rain due to dissolved SO₂ and NO₂ gases.
metadata.examinerTip: Normal rain has pH ~5.6 due to dissolved CO₂ forming H₂CO₃.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What color does phenolphthalein indicator turn in NaOH solution and in HCl solution?

metadata.modelAnswer: Phenolphthalein turns deep pink/magenta in basic NaOH solution, and remains colorless in acidic HCl solution.
metadata.examinerTip: Synthetic indicator widely used in acid-base titrations.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the color of methyl orange indicator in acidic and basic solutions?

metadata.modelAnswer: Methyl orange is red in acidic medium (pH < 3.1) and yellow in basic/neutral medium (pH > 4.4).
metadata.examinerTip: Original color in bottle is orange.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction of Zinc with dilute HCl.

metadata.modelAnswer: Zn (s) + 2HCl (aq) → ZnCl₂ (aq) + H₂ (g)↑.
metadata.examinerTip: State symbols (s, aq, g) show good chemistry rigor.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What product is formed when Zinc reacts with hot concentrated NaOH solution?

metadata.modelAnswer: Sodium Zincate (Na₂ZnO₂) and Hydrogen gas are formed: Zn + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂↑.
metadata.examinerTip: This demonstrates the amphoteric chemical nature of Zinc.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does Hydrogen gas burn with a characteristic 'pop' sound?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because Hydrogen rapidly combines with atmospheric Oxygen in a mini-explosive combustion reaction: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + Energy.
metadata.examinerTip: The pop sound is the acoustic shockwave of rapid expansion.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does Copper metal NOT liberate H₂ gas when treated with dilute HCl?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because Copper lies below Hydrogen in the reactivity series and cannot reduce H⁺ ions to H₂ gas.
metadata.examinerTip: E° of Cu²⁺/Cu (+0.34V) is more positive than H⁺/H₂ (0.00V).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is H₂ gas NOT evolved when metals react with dilute Nitric Acid (HNO₃)?

metadata.modelAnswer: HNO₃ is a strong oxidizing agent. It oxidizes the evolved H₂ into H₂O and itself gets reduced to nitrogen oxides (NO, NO₂).
metadata.examinerTip: Only Magnesium (Mg) and Manganese (Mn) liberate H₂ with extremely dilute 1% HNO₃.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What are olfactory indicators? Give two examples.

metadata.modelAnswer: Substances whose odor changes in acidic or basic media. Examples: Onion extract, Clove oil, Vanilla essence.
metadata.examinerTip: Their characteristic smell disappears in basic medium (NaOH).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why should sour substances like curd and lemon juice never be kept in copper or brass vessels?

metadata.modelAnswer: Organic acids in curd react with copper/brass to form toxic, poisonous metal salts that cause food poisoning.
metadata.examinerTip: Tin coating (Kalai) prevents this chemical attack.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What are amphoteric oxides? Give two examples.

metadata.modelAnswer: Metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to produce salt and water. Examples: Aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) and Zinc oxide (ZnO).
metadata.examinerTip: ZnO + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂O; ZnO + 2NaOH → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂O.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does dry HCl gas not turn dry blue litmus paper red?

metadata.modelAnswer: Acids manifest acidic properties only in the presence of water due to formation of hydronium ions (H₃O⁺). Dry HCl gas lacks free H⁺ ions.
metadata.examinerTip: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the difference between a base and an alkali?

metadata.modelAnswer: All alkalis are water-soluble bases (e.g. NaOH, KOH), but not all bases are soluble in water (e.g. Cu(OH)₂, Fe(OH)₃).
metadata.examinerTip: All alkalis are bases, but all bases are not alkalis.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is acid-base neutralization reaction always exothermic?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because H⁺ ions and OH⁻ ions combine to form stable covalent H₂O molecules, releasing ~57.1 kJ/mol of heat energy.
metadata.examinerTip: Heat of neutralization for strong acid + strong base is constant (-57.1 kJ).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why should water never be added directly into concentrated acid during dilution?

metadata.modelAnswer: The dilution is highly exothermic. Adding water to acid generates intense localized steam that splashes corrosive acid out of the beaker.
metadata.examinerTip: Rule: Always add Acid to Water slowly with constant stirring.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What type of reaction occurs when water is added to quicklime (CaO)?

metadata.modelAnswer: A highly exothermic combination reaction forming slaked lime [Ca(OH)₂].
metadata.examinerTip: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + Heat.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What color change is observed when green FeSO₄ crystals are heated?

metadata.modelAnswer: Green FeSO₄·7H₂O first turns white upon losing water of crystallization, then turns reddish-brown ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃) with evolution of SO₂ and SO₃ gases.
metadata.examinerTip: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does the blue color of CuSO₄ fade when iron nails are placed in it?

metadata.modelAnswer: More reactive Iron displaces Copper from CuSO₄ to form light-green ferrous sulphate (FeSO₄) solution.
metadata.examinerTip: Fe + CuSO₄ (blue) → FeSO₄ (green) + Cu (red-brown deposit).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is a double displacement reaction? Give the BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ example.

metadata.modelAnswer: A reaction in which two compounds exchange ions to form two new compounds, one of which is an insoluble precipitate (BaSO₄).
metadata.examinerTip: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ (white ppt) + 2NaCl.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What gas produces brown fumes when Lead Nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] powder is heated?

metadata.modelAnswer: Nitrogen Dioxide gas (NO₂) produces characteristic brown fumes.
metadata.examinerTip: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO (yellow) + 4NO₂↑ (brown) + O₂↑.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is Silver Chloride (AgCl) stored in dark amber-colored bottles?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because AgCl undergoes photolytic decomposition in sunlight into grey silver metal and chlorine gas: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂.
metadata.examinerTip: Used in black-and-white photography.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, identify the substance oxidized and reduced.

metadata.modelAnswer: Hydrogen (H₂) is oxidized to H₂O (gains oxygen). Copper oxide (CuO) is reduced to Cu (loses oxygen).
metadata.examinerTip: CuO acts as the oxidizing agent; H₂ acts as the reducing agent.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is rancidity and how is it prevented in packaged potato chips?

metadata.modelAnswer: Rancidity is the slow oxidation of fats and oils producing unpleasant smell and taste. Packaged food is flushed with unreactive Nitrogen gas.
metadata.examinerTip: Nitrogen acts as an inert atmosphere preventing atmospheric oxygen contact.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What chemical formula represents rust on iron objects?

metadata.modelAnswer: Hydrated Ferric Oxide: Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.
metadata.examinerTip: Requires both oxygen (O₂) and moisture (H₂O) simultaneously.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Give one example of an endothermic decomposition reaction.

metadata.modelAnswer: Decomposition of limestone (CaCO₃) upon heating to form quicklime (CaO) and CO₂.
metadata.examinerTip: CaCO₃ + Heat → CaO + CO₂.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why is cellular respiration considered an exothermic process?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because glucose reacts with oxygen in body cells to release energy (ATP) along with CO₂ and H₂O.
metadata.examinerTip: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Energy.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the color of the precipitate formed when Lead Nitrate reacts with Potassium Iodide?

metadata.modelAnswer: A bright yellow precipitate of Lead Iodide (PbI₂) is formed: Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂↓ + 2KNO₃.
metadata.examinerTip: Famous golden rain precipitation experiment.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Arrange Al, Zn, Fe, and Cu in order of decreasing chemical reactivity.

metadata.modelAnswer: Aluminium (Al) > Zinc (Zn) > Iron (Fe) > Copper (Cu).
metadata.examinerTip: Aluminium is most reactive; Copper is least reactive among the four.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why does Aluminium metal react slowly initially despite being very reactive?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because Aluminium forms a tough, non-porous protective oxide film (Al₂O₃) on its surface when exposed to air.
metadata.examinerTip: Cleaning with sandpaper removes this oxide barrier.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is the Thermite process used for joining railway tracks?

metadata.modelAnswer: Reduction of iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) by aluminium powder: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe (molten). Heat generated melts iron to weld tracks.
metadata.examinerTip: Exothermic displacement reaction producing liquid metal.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What metal coating is applied during galvanization to prevent iron rusting?

metadata.modelAnswer: A thin sacrificial layer of Zinc metal is applied onto iron objects.
metadata.examinerTip: Zinc oxidizes preferentially even if the surface coating is scratched.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Name one metal that is liquid at room temperature and one non-metal liquid at room temperature.

metadata.modelAnswer: Liquid metal: Mercury (Hg). Liquid non-metal: Bromine (Br₂).
metadata.examinerTip: Gallium and Caesium melt just above room temp (~30°C).

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is anodizing of aluminium objects?

metadata.modelAnswer: An electrochemical process that thickens the natural protective aluminium oxide layer by making aluminium the anode during electrolysis of dilute H₂SO₄.
metadata.examinerTip: Thickened oxide layer accepts colorful decorative dyes.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is Aqua Regia and what is the ratio of its constituent concentrated acids?

metadata.modelAnswer: A freshly prepared mixture of Concentrated HCl and Concentrated HNO₃ in a 3:1 ratio.
metadata.examinerTip: Capable of dissolving noble metals like Gold and Platinum.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What is an amalgam?

metadata.modelAnswer: An alloy in which one of the component metals is Mercury (e.g. Sodium amalgam Na-Hg, Dental amalgam).
metadata.examinerTip: Used as reducing agents and tooth fillings.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Differentiate between roasting and calcination in metallurgy.

metadata.modelAnswer: Roasting heats sulfide ores in excess air (2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂); Calcination heats carbonate ores in limited/no air (ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂).
metadata.examinerTip: Roasting = Sulfide ores + O₂; Calcination = Carbonate ores - O₂.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Why do ionic compounds (like NaCl) have high melting points?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because a large amount of energy is required to break strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions in the 3D crystal lattice.
metadata.examinerTip: Conducts electricity in molten/aqueous state, but not in solid state.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: Name the primary ore of Mercury metal and write its formula.

metadata.modelAnswer: Cinnabar, chemical formula Mercuric Sulfide (HgS).
metadata.examinerTip: Heated in air directly to yield Mercury metal: 2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂; 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂.

items.subject: Chemistry
items.body: What are the constituent elements of Brass and Bronze alloys?

metadata.modelAnswer: Brass: Copper (Cu) + Zinc (Zn). Bronze: Copper (Cu) + Tin (Sn).
metadata.examinerTip: Solder alloy is Lead (Pb) + Tin (Sn).

items.subject: Physics
items.body: State Ohm's Law.

metadata.modelAnswer: Electric current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to potential difference (V) across its ends, provided temperature and physical conditions remain constant.
metadata.examinerTip: V ∝ I ⟹ V = IR.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Why is an ammeter always connected in series and a voltmeter in parallel?

metadata.modelAnswer: Ammeter has very low resistance so it measures total current without altering circuit resistance. Voltmeter has very high resistance so it draws negligible current when measuring potential difference.
metadata.examinerTip: Ideal ammeter resistance = 0; Ideal voltmeter resistance = ∞.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What does the slope of a V-I graph represent when V is plotted on Y-axis and I on X-axis?

metadata.modelAnswer: The slope (ΔV/ΔI) represents the electrical resistance (R) of the conductor.
metadata.examinerTip: If I is on Y-axis and V on X-axis, slope represents conductance (1/R).

items.subject: Physics
items.body: State four factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.

metadata.modelAnswer: 1. Length of conductor (L); 2. Area of cross-section (A); 3. Nature of material (Resistivity ρ); 4. Temperature.
metadata.examinerTip: R = ρ L / A.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is resistivity (specific resistance) and what is its SI unit?

metadata.modelAnswer: Resistivity is the resistance of a conductor of unit length (1m) and unit cross-sectional area (1m²). Its SI unit is Ohm-meter (Ω·m).
metadata.examinerTip: Resistivity depends only on material and temperature, NOT on dimensions.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is the function of a rheostat in an electrical circuit?

metadata.modelAnswer: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to adjust or control current in a circuit without changing voltage source.
metadata.examinerTip: Works by varying effective length of high-resistance wire.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Give two examples of non-Ohmic conductors that do not follow Ohm's Law.

metadata.modelAnswer: Semiconductor Diodes, Transistors, Filament bulbs at high temperatures, Electrolytes.
metadata.examinerTip: Their V-I graph is curved rather than a straight line.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: How does resistance of a metallic wire change when its temperature increases?

metadata.modelAnswer: Resistance increases with temperature because thermal vibrations of metal ions increase, increasing electron collision frequency.
metadata.examinerTip: Alloys like Manganin and Constantan have near-zero temperature coefficient of resistance.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: How do you calculate the Least Count of an ammeter having 0-1A range with 20 divisions?

metadata.modelAnswer: Least Count = Total Range / Total Divisions = 1.0 A / 20 = 0.05 A per division.
metadata.examinerTip: Least count is the minimum value readable on the instrument scale.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Why should current NOT be passed continuously through the resistance wire for long durations?

metadata.modelAnswer: Continuous current heats up the wire due to Joule heating (H = I²Rt), which increases its resistance and causes deviations from Ohm's Law.
metadata.examinerTip: Remove key between readings to maintain constant temperature.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: If a resistance wire is stretched to double its length, what happens to its resistance?

metadata.modelAnswer: Resistance increases 4 times (4R). Stretching doubles length (L' = 2L) and halves area (A' = A/2), so R' = ρ(2L)/(A/2) = 4(ρL/A) = 4R.
metadata.examinerTip: Volume remains constant during stretching: A·L = A'·L'.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Why are standard resistance coils made of alloys like Manganin or Constantan instead of copper?

metadata.modelAnswer: Because Manganin and Constantan have very high resistivity and negligible temperature coefficient of resistance.
metadata.examinerTip: Their resistance stays constant even when warm.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is the equivalent resistance when two resistors R₁ and R₂ are connected in series?

metadata.modelAnswer: R_s = R₁ + R₂. The equivalent resistance is greater than the individual largest resistance.
metadata.examinerTip: Current (I) remains constant through series components.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is the equivalent resistance when two resistors R₁ and R₂ are connected in parallel?

metadata.modelAnswer: 1/R_p = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ ⟹ R_p = (R₁ R₂) / (R₁ + R₂). Equivalent resistance is smaller than the individual smallest resistance.
metadata.examinerTip: Voltage (V) remains constant across parallel branches.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Why are domestic household appliances connected in parallel rather than in series?

metadata.modelAnswer: 1. Each appliance gets full supply voltage (220V); 2. Each appliance operates independently with its own switch; 3. Total resistance is minimized.
metadata.examinerTip: In series, if one bulb fuses, the entire household circuit breaks.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is the total resistance of 'n' identical resistors each of resistance 'R' connected in parallel?

metadata.modelAnswer: Equivalent resistance R_p = R / n.
metadata.examinerTip: For 'n' identical in series, R_s = nR.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is the ratio of maximum resistance (R_s) to minimum resistance (R_p) for 'n' identical resistors?

metadata.modelAnswer: R_s / R_p = (n R) / (R / n) = n².
metadata.examinerTip: For 2 resistors, ratio is 4:1.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: State Joule's Law of Heating and give its mathematical expression.

metadata.modelAnswer: Heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to square of current (I²), resistance (R), and time (t): H = I²Rt Joules.
metadata.examinerTip: Alternative forms: H = VIt = (V²/R)t.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What properties should an electric fuse wire possess?

metadata.modelAnswer: High electrical resistivity and low melting point (e.g. Lead-Tin alloy).
metadata.examinerTip: Fuse is connected in series with live wire.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: What is electrical power and what are its three common mathematical formulas?

metadata.modelAnswer: Power is rate of electrical energy consumption. Formulas: P = VI, P = I²R, P = V²/R.
metadata.examinerTip: SI unit = Watt (W) = 1 Joule/second.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: Convert 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh) into Joules.

metadata.examinerTip: 1 kWh is commonly called 1 Unit of electricity.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: In a series circuit of 5Ω and 10Ω resistors connected to 15V battery, what is the current through the 10Ω resistor?

metadata.modelAnswer: Total R = 15Ω. Total I = 15V/15Ω = 1 A. Current is same (1 A) through both resistors in series.
metadata.examinerTip: Same current flows through all series components.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: In a parallel circuit of 6Ω and 12Ω connected to 12V battery, what is the voltage across the 6Ω resistor?

metadata.modelAnswer: Voltage is 12 V. In parallel, voltage across each branch equals the source battery voltage.
metadata.examinerTip: Branch current I₁ = 12/6 = 2A; I₂ = 12/12 = 1A.

items.subject: Physics
items.body: How can a sensitive galvanometer be converted into an ammeter?

metadata.modelAnswer: By connecting a very low resistance wire (called a Shunt) in parallel with the galvanometer coil.
metadata.examinerTip: To convert to voltmeter, connect high resistance in series.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What are stomata and where are they predominantly located on a dicot leaf?

metadata.modelAnswer: Stomata are microscopic pores on leaf surfaces. In dicots, they are predominantly located on the lower epidermis (hypostomatic).
metadata.examinerTip: In monocots, stomata are equally distributed on both surfaces (amphistomatic).

items.subject: Biology
items.body: Explain how guard cells control the opening and closing of stomatal pores.

metadata.modelAnswer: When water flows into guard cells, they become turgid and swell; their thick inner walls curve outwards, opening the pore. When guard cells lose water, they become flaccid and close the pore.
metadata.examinerTip: Driven by K⁺ ion accumulation and osmotic water influx.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: Why is Safranine stain used when preparing the leaf peel mount?

metadata.modelAnswer: Safranine stains plant cell walls and nuclei red/pink, creating sharp contrast for clear microscopic visualization.
metadata.examinerTip: It specifically stains lignified and suberized cell walls.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What is the role of glycerine in mounting the specimen on a glass slide?

metadata.modelAnswer: Glycerine acts as a mounting medium that prevents the peel specimen from drying out under light illumination and improves optical clarity.
metadata.examinerTip: Has a refractive index close to glass.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: Do epidermal cells contain chloroplasts? How do guard cells differ?

metadata.modelAnswer: General epidermal cells do NOT contain chloroplasts and are colorless. Guard cells ARE specialized epidermal cells that contain prominent green chloroplasts.
metadata.examinerTip: Guard cells produce glucose via photosynthesis to alter turgor pressure.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What is transpiration and what is its dual importance to plants?

metadata.modelAnswer: Transpiration is loss of water vapor from aerial parts of plants. Importance: 1. Creates transpirational pull for ascent of sap; 2. Cools leaf surfaces.
metadata.examinerTip: Described as a 'necessary evil' by Curtis.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What is the shape of guard cells in dicot plants versus monocot grasses?

metadata.modelAnswer: In dicots, guard cells are Kidney-shaped or Bean-shaped. In monocot grasses, guard cells are Dumbbell-shaped.
metadata.examinerTip: Classic practical viva comparison question.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What instrument is used to measure the rate of transpiration in plants?

metadata.modelAnswer: Ganong's Potometer.
metadata.examinerTip: Measures water intake rate by tracking air bubble movement.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What color change occurs on blue Cobalt Chloride paper during transpiration test?

metadata.modelAnswer: Dry blue Cobalt Chloride paper turns Pink when it absorbs transpired water vapor.
metadata.examinerTip: Pink color confirms presence of water moisture.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: What are sunken stomata and which ecological group of plants possesses them?

metadata.modelAnswer: Stomata located deep inside pits or grooves to minimize water loss. Possessed by Xerophytic desert plants (e.g. Nerium, Opuntia).
metadata.examinerTip: Adaptation for water conservation in arid habitats.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: Why is KOH (Potassium Hydroxide) placed inside the bell jar during photosynthesis experiments?

metadata.modelAnswer: KOH absorbs all carbon dioxide gas inside the enclosed space: 2KOH + CO₂ → K₂CO₃ + H₂O.
metadata.examinerTip: Used in Moll's half-leaf experiment to prove CO₂ is essential for photosynthesis.

items.subject: Biology
items.body: How and why is a potted plant destarched before photosynthesis experiments?

metadata.modelAnswer: By keeping the potted plant in a completely dark room for 48-72 hours. This ensures all existing starch in leaves is consumed by respiration.
metadata.examinerTip: Prevents false-positive iodine starch test results.
